stops.note: from mola 'millstone'; Vitruvius had already described a geared water mill in his De architectura around 20s BC
borrowed via West Germanic (German Mühle); the Domesday Book of 1086 counts about 5,600 mills in England
extended to factories, as in the Lancashire cotton mills of the Industrial Revolution after the 1770s

current_meaning: a building with machinery for grinding grain; a factory
